name: upgrade-catalog-roll-forward
body:
source: v0.10.0 release defect — `kalide upgrade` did not refresh the AGENTS.md guides for a project from the previous release. A deck created/last-upgraded by v0.9.0 carries `deck:AGENTS.md` digest 4ee150bbf809ab5d42952a78b5f5892378ce2988231f669faf77682d48cc2d70; a v0.9.0 library carries `library:AGENTS.md` digest 53513b1643dcffa67d633ca5aa45177c1ac2f37a85aacd802a6ab70b2bf44511. The running v0.10.0 binary's `scaffoldversions.json` (internal/scaffold/scaffoldversions.json) carries NO `v0.9.0` entry for either identity: the digest that commit 08b406e6 (""Release v0.9.0"") left labelled `"unreleased"` was OVERWRITTEN in place by the 0.10.0 doc commits 586c13ec/b72aa0ca with the new digest. Before/after in the catalog: `deck:AGENTS.md` went from a `2ef9099e…` / `["unreleased"]` entry to the new digest (no `v0.9.0` label survives); `library:AGENTS.md` likewise. Consequence: `catalogLookup` (internal/scaffold/catalog.go) is identity+digest scoped, so a v0.9.0 guide matches no catalogued digest of its identity, `refreshMember` (internal/scaffold/refresh.go) classifies it as author content and reports it skipped (`refreshed (0)`), violating this constraint's ""every tagged kalide release"" coverage clause and the AC of requirements.requirement.upgrade-refresh-owned-scaffold (""a deck scaffolded by a previous kalide with an unmodified old AGENTS.md ends with the current guide after upgrade"").

inconsistency: the constraint said the catalog is ""regenerated and extended for each release"" but never forbade REPLACING a digest that already carried a released version label — the exact overwrite-in-place that dropped v0.9.0's bytes from coverage. The roll-forward obligation (move the prior `unreleased` digest to the just-released tag, THEN add the new digest) was implicit and was not followed.

resolution [autonomous]: do NOT weaken the requirement or the covering constraint. Sharpen global.constraint.upgrade-known-version-catalog with an explicit ""Roll-forward (never overwrite a released digest)"" paragraph: a release that changes a scaffold file MUST roll the prior `unreleased` digest forward to the just-released tag and keep it, adding the new digest alongside — never overwrite it; a released version label may never be dropped or reassigned to different bytes, and every tag in a digest's ""which releases ship it"" list must stay resolvable to that tag's shipped bytes. The code fix itself (restoring the two v0.9.0 digests under `v0.9.0` alongside the new digest) is the plan/implementation's job, not this reconciliation's.
